title: Laschamp geomagnetic excursion
summary: The Laschamp event was a short excursion of the Earth's magnetic field, named for its type site in the Massif Central of France. Paleomagnetic study with K/Ar and 40Ar/39Ar dating of 37 lava flows in the Chaîne des Puys puts it at 41.3 ± 0.6 thousand years ago, lasting under a thousand years. It has been found in sediments and lavas worldwide and may serve as a geochronological marker.

uncertainty.note: Laj et al. (EGU 2014): 41.3 ± 0.6 ka (2 sigma); Sier et al. (2024): around 41 ka BP, duration under one thousand years. ka values are used as stated, with no 1950 offset applied.

as_recorded.value: ~41 ka BP; duration of less than one thousand years

where.modern_name: Chaîne des Puys, Massif Central, France (type site area; the event is recorded worldwide)
where.historical_name: Volcanic chain in what is now central France; no polities or place names exist at this date

importance.justification: A well-dated global magnetic marker, used to tie together sediment, ice-core and archaeological chronologies.

sources.title: Dynamics of the Earth Magnetic Field during the period of high variability covering the Laschamp and Mono Lake excursions (EGU2014-2340)
